guideTitle: 5 Best GE Motion Sensor Night Lights in 2026
metaTitle: Best GE Motion Sensor Night Lights in 2026
metaDescription: Five GE plug-in motion sensor night lights compared by brightness, pack size and finish, so you can light a hallway or bath without fuss.
introParagraphs: GE is one of the most familiar names in household lighting, and its motion sensor night lights share a simple idea: plug one in, and a small LED comes on when someone walks past in the dark. There is no app, no battery door and no setup menu. The differences between the models are real but easy to miss on a store shelf, because most of them look like a white or bronze rectangle with a sensor window.

We evaluated five GE motion lights that are plainly built around movement sensing: the 2-pack at 40 lumens, the single 20 lumen light, the Ultra Brite single at 40 lumens, the bronze 40 lumen version and the Ultrabrite light bar at 100 lumens. Most of the 40 lumen and 20 lumen models list the same motion reach of up to 25 feet and the same 90 second shut-off, so the choice comes down to brightness, pack size, finish and how much light you want at 2 a.m.

A night light is a comfort and convenience product, not a safety system. These GE models are good at making a dark hall or bathroom less jarring, and the guide below explains which one fits which room.

products.name: GE Plug-In Motion Sensor Night Light, 2 Pack, 40 Lumens
products.description:
The two-pack is the easiest GE recommendation because it solves the usual problem of needing a light in more than one spot. Each unit puts out 40 lumens of warm 3000K white, which is bright enough to show a floor and soft enough that it does not feel like switching on a lamp. The listing gives a motion reach of up to 25 feet, which is long for a plug-in night light and suits a hallway or a kitchen.

Two sensing jobs happen at once. A dusk-to-dawn light sensor keeps the lamp off in daylight and in a lit room, and the motion sensor brings it on only when you move. It then holds the light for 90 seconds after the last movement, a comfortable window that avoids the light snapping off while you are still halfway across the room. There is no dimmer, so the 40 lumens is what you get.

In use, the pack is plug-and-forget. Put one near the bedroom door and one in the bathroom, and the house stays dark except where you walk. Compared with the single 20 lumen GE it is twice as bright, and compared with the 100 lumen light bar it is much gentler. The trade is that 40 lumens can feel bright in a very small bedroom, and each light needs a free outlet at a useful height.
products.bestFor: Households that want two rooms covered with a trusted, simple light.
cons: 40 lumens is bright in tiny rooms

products.name: GE LED Motion Sensor Night Light, 20 Lumens
products.description:
The 20 lumen GE is the gentlest light in this group, and that is exactly its appeal. At half the output of the 40 lumen models it gives a soft pool of soft white light that shows the edge of the bed and the path to the door without lighting up the whole room. People who sleep lightly, or who share a room, often prefer this lower level.

The sensing is the same as its brighter siblings: motion reach of up to 25 feet, a 90 second shut-off after movement stops and a dusk-to-dawn sensor that keeps it off by day. The housing is compact and plugs in so that the second outlet stays usable, which matters in a bedroom where outlets are already crowded. The LED is long-life and cool to the touch, so there is no bulb to replace.

Where it falls short is in a long hall or a larger bathroom, where 20 lumens will look dim next to the 40 lumen GE two-pack. It also comes as a single light, so a second room means buying another. Pick it for the bedroom, the nursery-style small space or any room where less light is the point, and use a brighter GE for the hallway.
products.bestFor: Small bedrooms and light sleepers who want the lowest glow.
pros: Softest output of the GE group

products.name: GE Ultra Brite Motion-Activated LED Night Light, 40 Lumens
products.description:
The Ultra Brite is the single-light version of the same 40 lumen idea found in the two-pack. It is described as suitable for hallways, bedrooms, bathrooms, kitchens and stairways, and that breadth is believable because 40 lumens sits in the middle of what a plug-in night light does well. It uses motion sensing out to 25 feet with a 90 second auto-off.

A dusk-to-dawn sensor keeps it quiet in daylight, so it will not trigger on a sunny afternoon, and it saves energy by only working in low light. The output is soft white, a touch less golden than the 3000K two-pack, and for most rooms the difference is small. The body is a low-profile white unit that blends with a wall plate and does not shout for attention.

The practical question is whether you need one light or two. If you only have a single dark spot, such as the hall outside the bathroom, this is the cheaper way in than the two-pack. If you already know you want two rooms covered, the two-pack gives you a second light for less than buying two singles. It shares the weaknesses of the family, namely no dimming and a need for an outlet at a decent height.
products.bestFor: One dark hallway or bathroom that needs a reliable light.
cons: Needs an outlet at useful height

products.name: GE Plug-In Motion Sensor Night Light, 40 Lumens, Bronze
products.description:
The bronze GE is the pick when the outlet cover is not white. Many older homes, and a lot of kitchens and dens, have brown or bronze plates, and a white night light stands out against them. This model keeps the same 40 lumen soft white output and the 25 foot motion reach, and simply changes the housing color. The listing also notes UL certification.

Everything else matches the white Ultra Brite. It senses darkness with a dusk-to-dawn sensor, wakes on motion, and holds for 90 seconds after the last movement. It plugs straight in and needs no battery. Because the output is identical, you give up nothing for the sake of appearance, which is not always true of decorative night lights.

The limits are the same too: no dimmer, one light per purchase and an outlet that must sit where the sensor can see you walk. Choose it over the white Ultra Brite only for looks, since the function is the same. If you are matching a whole home, buy this alongside a white unit for the rooms with white plates.
products.bestFor: Rooms with bronze or brown outlet plates where white looks out of place.
pros: Bronze housing hides on dark plates
cons: Same function as the white model

products.name: GE Ultrabrite Plug-In LED Night Light Bar, 100 Lumens, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Ultrabrite light bar is a different animal from the other four GE lights. At 100 lumens each, it is two and a half times as bright as the 40 lumen models, and the long bar shape spreads light along a wall. The listing points to hallways, kitchens and garages, which are places where a faint glow is not enough.

An On, Off and Auto switch gives it more control than the fixed GE models. Auto is the motion mode, which detects movement in low light; On makes it a steady light, and Off silences it. That switch makes the bar useful as a task light in a garage or laundry room, not only as a bedroom night light.

The price of that brightness is glare. In a bedroom 100 lumens will wake a light sleeper, so keep it out of sleeping spaces. The listing does not publish a motion range or a fixed shut-off time, so place it close to your path and see how it behaves. For a bright, work-friendly motion light in a hall or garage, it is the strongest GE here, while the 20 lumen light is the opposite choice for bedrooms.
products.bestFor: Garages, laundry rooms and kitchens that need real light.
pros: Doubles as a steady task light

buyingCriteria.explanation: Brightness is the first thing to settle, because night lights vary more than they look. The GE 20 lumen light is the gentlest here, the 40 lumen models sit in the middle and the Ultrabrite bar reaches 100 lumens. For a bedroom, 20 lumens usually avoids waking a partner, while a hallway or kitchen is comfortable at 40. Remember that cool surfaces and glossy floors reflect more light, so a bright light in a tiled bathroom feels brighter than the number suggests.

Most of the GE lights list motion reach up to 25 feet and a 90 second shut-off, which is on the generous side for plug-ins. Reach decides how early the light comes on as you approach, and hold time decides whether it stays on while you finish a slow walk. A 90 second hold is comfortable, while a 20 second hold can drop out mid-trip. The light bar does not publish either figure, so treat it as a placement-by-trial product.

Count the places you walk in the dark, such as the bedroom door, hall and bathroom. The GE two-pack covers two of them in one purchase, while the 20 lumen light, the Ultra Brite and the bronze model are singles. Buying singles for three rooms costs more than a two-pack plus one single. Plan the full list before you shop so you do not end up with mismatched finishes.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Outlet position and the second socket
buyingCriteria.explanation: A plug-in light is only as good as its outlet. Low outlets put the sensor near the floor, where it may miss a standing figure or react to a pet. The GE 20 lumen light is designed to leave the second outlet free, which matters in crowded bedrooms. Check that the outlet is not behind furniture, because a blocked sensor window cuts the detection range.

Warm light is easier on the eyes at night. The GE two-pack states warm white 3000K, and the others are described as soft white. Cool white looks crisp in a store but is harsh when you wake at 2 a.m. If the listing does not give a Kelvin number, assume soft white is closer to 3000K than 5000K and judge by eye after plugging it in.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Finish and fit with your wall plates
buyingCriteria.explanation: A night light stays on the wall for years, so appearance matters more than it seems. The bronze GE model suits brown or bronze plates, while the white units blend with standard white outlets. A decorative option is not necessary for function, but a mismatched finish can make a tidy room look unfinished. Choose the finish by the plate color in the room where it will live.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brightness fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated output across the group: 20 lumens for the gentlest GE, 40 lumens for the two-pack, Ultra Brite and bronze models, and 100 lumens for the Ultrabrite bar. Each level was judged for the rooms it suits, with bedrooms favoring the low end and garages favoring the high end. We rewarded options that cover a clear use, not just those with the biggest number.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensing and timing
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the listed motion reach of up to 25 feet, the 90 second hold and the dusk-to-dawn sensor on the main models. Where a listing publishes no range or timer, as with the light bar, we noted that and scored it more cautiously. Consistent behavior matters because a light that drops out early is irritating.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of setup and use
howWeEvaluated.description: Every pick plugs into a standard outlet and needs no battery or app, so setup is nearly equal. We gave extra credit to the On, Off and Auto switch on the light bar and to the compact body of the 20 lumen light that leaves the second outlet open. Simple operation is central for a product people install once and forget.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value across pack sizes
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how much coverage each purchase gives. The two-pack and the two-bar set cover multiple rooms, while the singles suit one spot. We avoided stating prices, since they change, and focused on lights per purchase and fit to need.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The two-pack leads for general use, the 20 lumen light for bedrooms, the Ultra Brite for a single hallway, the bronze model for matching plates and the Ultrabrite bar for brightness. Putting each pick against its sibling made it clear where a GE light is genuinely different, and where it is merely a color change.

faq.q: Which GE motion sensor night light is brightest?
faq.a: The Ultrabrite light bar is the brightest here at 100 lumens per light, compared with 40 lumens for the two-pack, Ultra Brite and bronze models and 20 lumens for the gentlest GE. That is a big jump, and it suits garages and kitchens better than bedrooms. For sleeping areas, the lower outputs are usually more comfortable.

faq.q: How long does the light stay on after I walk past?
faq.a: The 40 lumen and 20 lumen GE models list a 90 second auto-off after motion stops. That is long enough for a slow walk to the bathroom and back. The light bar does not publish a fixed timer, so watch how it behaves after you install it.

faq.q: Is a two-pack better value than buying singles?
faq.a: If you need two rooms covered, yes, because the two-pack gives you a second 40 lumen light without a second purchase. If you have only one dark spot, a single Ultra Brite or the bronze model avoids paying for a light you will not use. Count your rooms first.

faq.q: Will the light come on during the day?
faq.a: No. The main GE models use a dusk-to-dawn sensor that keeps them off when a room is bright. They only react to motion when it is dark enough. One side effect is that a hallway lamp left on can stop the night light from triggering.

faq.q: Do these lights need batteries or an app?
faq.a: No. They plug straight into a standard outlet and run on household power, with a long-life LED. That means nothing to charge and no bulb to swap. The trade-off is that you need an outlet where you want the light.

faq.q: Can I use a GE night light on a stairway?
faq.a: The listings name stairways as a suitable place, but remember outlets are near the floor and may not sit where you need the light. A night light is a convenience and not a safety device. Keep the stairs clear and use a handrail, and consider lights made for steps if you want coverage at both ends.

faq.q: What is the difference between the white and bronze 40 lumen models?
faq.a: The finish. Both list 40 lumens, soft white light, motion reach up to 25 feet and a 90 second auto-off. Choose the bronze model when your outlet plates are bronze or brown, and the white Ultra Brite when they are white.
